description: Fall armyworm is a destructive caterpillar pest that attacks maize and many other crops. Larvae feed on leaves and growing points, causing severe crop damage and yield loss.
symptoms: Irregular holes and chewing damage on leaves
Large ragged holes in maize leaves
Severely damaged or destroyed plant growing point
spread: Adult moth migration over long distances
Egg masses laid on crop leaves
management: Regular field scouting for early detection
Hand removal of larvae in small fields
biological_control: Predators such as lady beetles and lacewings
Entomopathogenic fungi such as Beauveria bassiana
prevention: Early planting to avoid peak infestation
